text:
Deduplicating by (user, item) leaves each item at most once per user: within-history exact-repeat coverage and next-item exact recurrence become zero when deduplication precedes splitting. A zero recurrence probe then reflects preprocessing, not absent recurring interests. “SASRec preprocessing” alone does not establish deduplication: the [original SASRec loader](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/util.py) appends every supplied interaction before splitting. Amazon’s [dataset documentation](https://mcauleylab.ucsd.edu/public_datasets/data/amazon/datasets.html) also distinguishes duplicate reviews arising from merged product variants. Measure per-category repeated-user fraction and duplicate-event fraction, (length − unique items)/length, on available histories before choosing exact recurrence as a primary probe.

For unique-item histories, a feasible proposed fallback is cross-item content recurrence: TF-IDF word/character n-grams over titles and descriptions, cosine similarity or clustering, and timestamps to distinguish nearby bursts from returns after intervening interests. [TF-IDF](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/feature_extraction.html#text-feature-extraction) requires no pretrained weights. Test model reliance by masking/removing earlier items in a recurring content group, retaining only that group, or shuffling its order while preserving membership. History deletion has precedent in [counterfactual recommendation explanations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09752); these interventions assess model sensitivity, not causal user intent.

Validate the proposed proxy through metadata coverage, inspection of matched titles, threshold stability, and comparisons against random interventions matched for count, position, recency and item popularity. Fit representations and thresholds without validation targets; use training-prefix next-item checks, then the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 for model selection. Report paired score/rank changes and uncertainty. Missing text means unavailable proxy evidence. Lexical recurrence may capture editions or boilerplate, so it cannot establish true intent, diversity or conformity.
